q: What is the rarest stamp in the world?
What is the British Guiana 1c Magenta?
What is the most valuable stamp ever sold?
Which stamp has only one known copy?
How much is the British Guiana 1c Magenta worth?
What is the story behind the world's rarest stamp?
a: The British Guiana 1c Magenta is the world's rarest and most valuable stamp, with only a single specimen known to exist. It was issued in 1856 as a provisional when a shipment of stamps from England was delayed, and the local postmaster commissioned a newspaper to print crude designs on magenta paper. The stamp was discovered in 1873 by a 12-year-old Scottish schoolboy who found it among his uncle's correspondence and sold it for a few shillings. It has since passed through renowned collections, most recently selling privately in 2014 for $9.48 million, making it the most valuable stamp ever sold.

q: What is the Treskilling Yellow?
What is the most valuable Swedish stamp?
What is the story of the Treskilling Yellow color error?
How much is the Treskilling Yellow worth?
What stamp has a famous color error?
Who discovered the Treskilling Yellow?
What makes the Treskilling Yellow so rare?
a: The Treskilling Yellow is Sweden's most famous and valuable stamp, a color error from the 1855 issue that should have been green but was mistakenly printed in yellow. Only one copy is known, making it one of the world's great stamp rarities. It was discovered in 1886 by a Swedish schoolboy who sold it to a dealer. The stamp last sold at auction in 2010 for over two million dollars, making it the second most valuable known stamp.

q: What are the Mauritius Post Office stamps?
What is the value of Mauritius Post Office stamps?
What is the story of the Mauritius Post Office stamps?
What are the blue and red Mauritius issues?
What is the Bordeaux cover?
How many Mauritius Post Office stamps survive?
What error appears on the Mauritius Post Office stamps?
a: The Mauritius 'Post Office' stamps of 1847 were the first stamps issued by a British colony outside Great Britain, featuring a profile of Queen Victoria and the error 'Post Office' instead of 'Post Paid' on the left panel. Two values were issued: an orange-red one-penny and a deep blue two-pence, with fewer than 30 examples of both colors known to survive today. The most famous piece of Mauritius philatelic history is the Bordeaux cover—an envelope franked with both the one-penny red and two-pence blue 'Post Office' stamps, discovered in 1896, which sold for $1.2 million in 1993 (then a world record for a cover). Individual 'Post Office' stamps have sold for over $1 million each at auction.

q: What is the Inverted Jenny?
What is the US 24c airmail invert stamp?
How much is the Inverted Jenny worth?
What is the story behind the upside-down airplane stamp?
What is the most famous US stamp error?
Who discovered the Inverted Jenny sheet?
How many Inverted Jenny stamps exist?
a: The Inverted Jenny is the most famous US stamp error, a 24-cent airmail stamp from 1918 featuring a Curtiss JN-4 biplane printed upside-down in the center. The error occurred when a sheet of 100 stamps was printed with an inverted center due to a paper misalignment in the two-color printing process. Only one sheet was discovered on May 14, 1918, by Washington DC stockbroker William Robey, who bought it at a post office counter and became an instant philatelic legend. The sheet was broken up soon after, with individual stamps now valued at up to half a million dollars depending on condition. A block of four sold for nearly five million dollars at auction in recent years.

q: What are the Hawaiian Missionaries stamps?
What is the value of Hawaiian Missionaries?
What is the story of Hawaii's earliest stamps?
What are the 2c blue, 5c blue, and 13c dark red Missionaries?
Why are the Hawaiian Missionaries so rare?
How many Hawaiian Missionaries stamps exist today?
Why are they called Missionary stamps?
a: The Hawaiian Missionaries (1851-1852) are among the world's rarest and most valuable stamps, issued during the Kingdom of Hawaii for use by missionaries corresponding with the mainland. Three denominations were produced: a 2-cent blue, 5-cent blue, and 13-cent dark red. The stamps were crudely printed on thin, brittle paper—most surviving examples show faults like thins and tears due to their fragility. The 2-cent blue missionary is the rarest, with only about 15 copies known, and a fine example sold at auction for $325,000 in 2021. The stamps derive their name from their primary users, Christian missionaries who sought to convert the Hawaiian population, and their extreme rarity stems from low print runs (as few as 500 of some denominations) and a devastating fire that destroyed the remaining stock.

q: What is the Basel Dove stamp?
What is the value of the Basel Dove?
What is the story of Switzerland's classic stamp?
What are the most famous Swiss stamps?
Why is the Basel Dove historically significant?
What was unique about the Basel Dove's printing?
How many Basel Dove stamps survive today?
a: The Basel Dove (Switzerland, 1845) is one of the world's most beautiful and famous classic stamps, issued by the Swiss canton of Basel. It was the world's first multicolored stamp (black, crimson, and blue) and the first to use a embossed design—a white dove carrying a letter in its beak, created by the architect Melchior Berri. Only 41,520 were printed, with a survival rate estimated at around 3,000-4,000 examples, making it genuinely rare. The stamp's elegant design, pioneering multicolor printing, and historical significance in Swiss philately make it one of the most sought-after classics, with fine used examples selling for $10,000-$30,000 and mint examples commanding much higher prices.

q: What are the most famous stamp errors and varieties?
What are inverted centers and missing colors?
What are missing perforations and color errors?
What are watermark errors in stamps?
What stamp printing errors are most valuable?
What causes missing perforation errors?
What modern US stamp error is collectible?
a: Stamp errors and varieties arise from printing, perforation, or paper mistakes during production and can dramatically increase a stamp's value. Major error types include: inverted centers (the design centerpiece printed upside-down, as in the Inverted Jenny and hundreds of other worldwide examples), missing colors (intentional design elements omitted in error), color errors (wrong color used for a denomination, like the Treskilling Yellow), missing perforations (stamps without perforations when they should have them, or imperforate errors), perforation shifts (perforations cutting into the design rather than between stamps), watermark varieties (inverted, sideways, or missing watermarks), and paper errors (using the wrong paper type). Some of the most valuable modern errors include the 2004 US 37-cent Flag stamp with the flag oriented incorrectly (called the 'Flag Over Porch' error), with an estimated 200 known examples.
